markscheme.html:
a

The rocket represents a non-inertial (accelerating) reference frame. [1 mark]

According to the Principle of Equivalence, the effects of a uniform acceleration are locally indistinguishable from the effects of a uniform gravitational field . Thus, the observer experiences a pseudo-force downward identical to weight. [1 mark]

b

During the finite time that it takes for the light signal to travel the distance from the source to the nose, the rocket (and thus the detector) gains additional velocity in the direction of acceleration. [1 mark]

Relative to the inertial frame in which the light was originally emitted, the detector is moving away from the point of emission at the time of reception. [1 mark]

This relative motion results in a longitudinal Doppler shift, causing the measured frequency to decrease (), a phenomenon known as redshift. [1 mark]

c

By the Principle of Equivalence, the redshift observed in the accelerating rocket must also occur in a stationary gravitational field. [1 mark]

Frequency corresponds to the rate of periodic events (ticks of a clock); since the frequency is lower at the top (nose) when sent from the bottom (rear), an observer at the top perceives the bottom clock to be ticking slower. [1 mark]

Therefore, time runs more slowly at lower gravitational potentials (closer to the center of mass) compared to higher gravitational potentials. [1 mark]
